data.command: Explain service manipulation T1543 for persistence

data.text:
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ ref attck T1543
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ pager /usr/share/doc/attck/T1543.txt
ATT&CK T1543 - Create or Modify System Process            (local ref snapshot)
==============================================================================
Platform scope : Linux / macOS / Windows
Use case       : Persistence (and occasionally Privilege Escalation)
Last sync      : 2024-11-08  (mirror: /usr/share/doc/attck/, offline copy)

DESCRIPTION
  Adversaries may create or modify system-level processes to repeatedly
  execute payloads at boot or at defined intervals. On Linux the practical
  targets are the init system and its unit files; the objective is a
  service that starts before/independent of the interactive session and
  survives reboot, package cleanup, and logoff.

SUB-TECHNIQUES
  T1543.001  Windows Service            (SCM / sc.exe / service registry keys)
  T1543.002  Systemd Service            (unit files, drop-ins, generators)
  T1543.004  Launch Daemon              (macOS plist under /Library/Launch*)

LINUX LANDING ZONES WORTH MONITORING
  /etc/systemd/system/.service           operator-authored units
  /usr/lib/systemd/system/.service       package-owned units (overwrite)
  /etc/systemd/system/.d/.conf          drop-in overrides
  ~/.config/systemd/user/.service        user-scope units (systemctl --user)
  /etc/init.d/, /etc/rc.d/, /etc/rc.local legacy init paths
  cron / at / anacron                     adjacent scheduling surface
  /etc/ld.so.preload, LD_PRELOAD wrappers indirect code injection

REPRESENTATIVE OBSERVABLES
  - unit created with ExecStart pointing at /tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp
  - Restart=always combined with a non-package binary path
  - systemctl enable <unit> or symlink materialising in
     /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/ outside a package change
  - systemd-analyze dump / daemon-reload events with no accompanying
     package manager transaction
  - file ownership root:root on a unit whose ExecStart is user-writable

DETECTION HOOKS
  auditd watch: -w /etc/systemd/system -p wa -k systemd_unit
  auditd watch: -w /usr/lib/systemd/system -p wa -k systemd_unit
  auditd watch: -w /etc/systemd/system -p wa -k systemd_dropin
  process create events: systemctl (enable|link|daemon-reload), timedatectl
  cluster the above against apt/dpkg/rpm write activity in the same window

MITIGATION SURFACE
  - restrict write access to unit directories to root (0555/0644 default)
  - enable and enforce SELinux/AppArmor confinement for service units
  - drop unused schedulers; audit rc.local and legacy init scripts
  - file integrity monitoring with baseline diff on unit directories
  - principle of least privilege for service accounts (no shell, no HOME
    write, ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges=yes)

RELATED
  T1053 Scheduled Task/Job     T1546 Event Triggered Execution
  T1547 Boot or Logon Autostart T1037 Boot or Logon Init Scripts
  T1055 Process Injection      T1574 Hijack Execution Flow

NOTE: local mirror is read-only. For the canonical text and full
      detection mappings see attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543.
